A.summary:
Posting a Patchwork check used to treat an empty patch lookup as
success, so no check was posted when Patchwork had not yet indexed the
patch. This change makes that case a distinct, retryable error, so the
worker retries until Patchwork catches up (fixes issue 461).

Before:
  When Patchwork returned an empty list for the Message-ID,
  post_patchwork_check returned Ok(()). The worker marked the outbox
  entry Sent although nothing was posted, while the review email
  still went out. Other failures were plain String errors, logged at
  error level.

After:
  An empty list returns Err(PatchworkCheckError::NotIndexedYet). The
  worker logs it at info level as "not ready yet" and retries it with
  the same three-attempt backoff used for other failures. If retries
  run out, the entry is marked failed with the error text. Real API
  or network failures become PatchworkCheckError::Api(String), still
  logged at error level and retried the same way.

The change adds the PatchworkCheckError enum, with Display and Error
implementations, in src/patchwork.rs. It changes the return type of
post_patchwork_check and updates the worker in
src/worker/patchwork.rs to match on the variant. Three tests are
added: one for the Display text, and two using a small raw-socket
HTTP server, checking that an empty 200 gives NotIndexedYet and that
a 500 gives Api.
A.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/worker/patchwork.rs (PatchworkWorker::run), the log level is
  chosen from the error variant alone, before the max_retries check. When the
  final attempt returns NotIndexedYet, the row is marked Failed through
  mark_patchwork_failed, but the only log line is info 'not ready yet'. The
  terminal loss of the Patchwork check never appears at error level, so
  operators watching error logs see nothing while the review email has
  already gone out (the issue 461 symptom). Log at error or warn whenever
  the row is marked Failed, whatever the variant.

- [MEDIUM] In src/worker/patchwork.rs (PatchworkWorker::run and
  backoff_seconds), NotIndexedYet shares the default 3-attempt budget
  (default_max_retries in src/settings.rs, passed from
  settings.review.max_retries in src/main.rs). Only the 5s and 30s delays
  are reachable, so the retry window is about 35s before the row becomes
  terminal Failed and is never selected again. If Patchwork's mirror lags
  longer, issue 461 (review email sent, no Patchwork status) still occurs,
  now recorded as Failed instead of a false Sent. The Fixes #461 claim is
  not backed by the diff, and the new tests never exercise the worker retry
  path. Use a separate, longer budget for NotIndexedYet (for example the
  180s tier) without changing the shared review and forge retry counts.

- [MEDIUM] In src/patchwork.rs (post_patchwork_check), every empty 200 list
  is returned as NotIndexedYet, and PatchworkWorker::run in
  src/worker/patchwork.rs gives it the same short budget as API errors. A
  patch not indexed within about 35s is dropped as Failed, and a permanently
  empty list cannot be told apart from mirror lag. The new tests only check
  single-request return values. Measure the real delay between review
  completion and the patch appearing in the msgid lookup, give NotIndexedYet
  its own longer backoff, and log at error level on the final failure.

findings.problem: final NotIndexedYet attempt marked Failed but logged at info
findings.explanation: Consequence: when the last allowed attempt returns NotIndexedYet, the outbox row goes to terminal Failed and the Patchwork check is never posted, while the review email has already gone out. That is the issue 461 symptom. The only log line for that attempt is info!("... not ready yet"). Reachability: any patch that Patchwork has not indexed by the third attempt, with the default max_retries of 3. Blast radius: one missing status per patch. It is recoverable because the reason is stored in the error_log column, but an operator watching error logs sees nothing. Mechanism: the match on &e chooses info! or error! from the variant alone, before the `entry.retry_count + 1 >= self.max_retries` check. mark_patchwork_failed then runs with no further log, and error! fires only if the DB write itself fails. The 'not ready yet' wording is also misleading on a terminal attempt. C18 says the old code logged this case at error!, but the old code returned Ok(()) and marked the row Sent, so that part is inaccurate. The visibility gap is still real. Fix: log at error or warn whenever the row is marked Failed, whatever the variant.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The log level depends only on the error variant, not on whether this attempt is the last one.
This is the terminal Failed transition, and it emits no error-level log for NotIndexedYet.

findings.problem: NotIndexedYet retry window is only about 35s before row is Failed
findings.explanation:
Consequence and reachability: when Sashiko finishes a review and Patchwork's mailing list mirror has not indexed the message within roughly 35 seconds, the Patchwork check is never posted. The row is marked Failed and never retried, so issue 461 (review email sent, no Patchwork status) still occurs for slow-mirror cases. The only change is that the loss is now recorded in error_log instead of a false Sent. This is reachable on every patchwork_outbox row handled by PatchworkWorker::run. Impact is one missing CI-style status per patch, which can be re-queued by hand, so it is not High. It is capped at Medium because the real mirror lag is unknown: neither the repo, docs/ nor the diff states it. If the lag is under about 35s the fix works; if it is minutes, it does not.

Verified chain. default_max_retries() returns 3 (src/settings.rs:810) and main.rs:920 passes settings.review.max_retries to PatchworkWorker::new, so the Patchwork worker shares the review retry budget. In PatchworkWorker::run, attempt 1 (retry_count 0): 0+1>=3 is false, so it schedules +5s (backoff_seconds(0)) and set_patchwork_retry_at increments retry_count to 1. Attempt 2 (retry_count 1): 2>=3 is false, so it schedules +30s and retry_count becomes 2. Attempt 3 (retry_count 2): 3>=3 is true, so mark_patchwork_failed runs and the status is terminal. The 180s tier (the _ arm of backoff_seconds) is unreachable at the default of 3. lock_pending_patchwork does honour next_retry_at (WHERE status = 'Pending' AND (next_retry_at IS NULL OR next_retry_at <= ?)), so the delays are real; total elapsed is about 35s plus worker polling granularity (5s idle sleep). A Failed row is never selected again.

The commit message claims Fixes #461, but the diff contains no evidence that the mirror catches up within this window. The new tests only use a one-shot server returning [] and check the enum variant; nothing exercises the worker's retry budget against NotIndexedYet. Confirming evidence would be measured Patchwork indexing lag from the issue or logs. The remedy is a separate, longer budget for NotIndexedYet (for example a dedicated limit or the 180s tier), without changing the shared review and forge retry counts.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Treats NotIndexedYet like any Api error and marks the row terminally Failed after 3 attempts.
Only the 5s and 30s delays are reachable with max_retries=3, giving about a 35s window.
Sets the default shared attempt budget.
Wires the generic review retry count into the Patchwork worker, so raising it would also affect review retries.
Confirms the backoff delays are honoured, so the window is genuinely about 35s and not shorter or longer.

findings.problem: NotIndexedYet retry window is about 35s, then check is dropped
findings.explanation: Consequence and reachability: after this change a Patchwork check for a patch that Patchwork's mirror has not indexed within about 35 seconds still never reaches Patchwork. The row ends as Failed, so issue 461 (review email sent, no Patchwork status) can persist. The failed check cannot be undone without manual re-queueing. It is reachable on every review completion: Reviewer::queue_notifications inserts a patchwork_outbox row, and PatchworkWorker::run polls it every 5s. Reasoning: the candidate's premise is only partly right. The empty-list case is bounded, and the final row is recorded as Failed with error_log, so it is not a silent success (that was the old Ok(()) bug). The api_url check does not catch the permanent cases. PatchworkPolicy::normalize only validates the scheme, and a 200 with [] for a valid host is not filtered earlier. But a permanent empty list costs only two extra requests and then a recorded failure, which is Low on its own. The real defect is in the retry budget. settings.review.max_retries defaults to 3 (default_max_retries). In PatchworkWorker::run the terminal condition is retry_count + 1 >= max_retries. backoff_seconds returns 5s for retry_count 0, 30s for retry_count 1, and the third attempt (retry_count 2) is terminal. The total wait is therefore about 35s plus request time. The doc comment and commit message treat NotIndexedYet as self-resolving through the three-attempt backoff, but a mailing-list mirror lag can plausibly exceed 35s. The 180s tier in backoff_seconds is never reached with the default max_retries. Nothing in the diff shows the window outlasts real indexing delay. The new tests only exercise the single-request return values, not the worker retry path. Second defect: on the final attempt, a NotIndexedYet error is logged only at info ("not ready yet") and then mark_patchwork_failed is called. The terminal failure is therefore never logged at error level, so log-based monitoring sees nothing when a check is permanently dropped. Cap at Medium: the 35s window versus real Patchwork indexing latency is an assumption about the external service. Confirm by measuring the delay between Sashiko completion and the patch appearing in Patchwork's /patches/?msgid= lookup. Fix direction: use a longer or separate backoff budget for NotIndexedYet, and log at error when the final attempt fails.

B.summary:
When Patchwork has not yet indexed a patch, looking it up by Message-ID
returns an empty list. Before this change, post_patchwork_check treated
that as success, so the worker marked the outbox entry Sent although no
check was ever posted. This change makes that case a distinct, retryable
error, so the existing three-attempt backoff retries it until Patchwork's
mailing list mirror catches up (fixes issue 461).

The function now returns a PatchworkCheckError enum with two variants:
NotIndexedYet for the empty-list case, and Api(String) for URL-building,
network, HTTP status and parse failures. The worker logs NotIndexedYet at
info level and Api errors at error level, and converts the error to a
string when recording a permanent failure in the database. The diff also
adds three tests: one for the error's Display text, and two that use a
one-shot raw-socket HTTP server to check that an empty 200 response
yields NotIndexedYet and that a 500 response yields Api.

Before:
  Patchwork returns 200 with [] for a patch it has not indexed yet.
  post_patchwork_check returns Ok(()), the outbox entry is marked Sent,
  and no check is ever posted. The review email goes out but Patchwork
  shows no status for the patch.

After:
  The same response returns Err(NotIndexedYet). The worker logs
  "Patchwork check ID <id> not ready yet" at info level and retries
  with the shared backoff. If the patch is still not indexed after the
  maximum retries, the entry is marked failed with the message
  "Patchwork has not indexed this message yet" instead of being
  silently marked Sent.

The outbox row ends Failed instead of the old false Sent, and nothing retries it. Every Patchwork-enabled review reaches this path via reviewer.rs insert_patchwork_outbox, then PatchworkWorker::run. The worker-level retry path (reschedule versus mark failed on NotIndexedYet) has no test. The new tests only cover post_patchwork_check returning the error variants. C.summary:
This change stops the Patchwork check poster from reporting success
when Patchwork has not yet indexed the patch. It adds a
PatchworkCheckError type with a NotIndexedYet variant, so the worker
retries that case through its existing three-attempt backoff instead
of marking the outbox entry Sent. This fixes issue 461, where a review
email went out but Patchwork never got a status for the patch.

Before:
  When the msgid lookup on Patchwork returned an empty list because
  its mailing list mirror had not caught up, post_patchwork_check
  returned Ok. The worker marked the outbox entry Sent although no
  check was posted, and it was never retried. Patchwork showed no
  status for a patch whose review email had already been delivered.

After:
  An empty lookup result returns Err(NotIndexedYet). The worker logs
  it at info level ("Patchwork check ID N not ready yet") and retries
  with the shared backoff. Once the patch is indexed, the check is
  posted and the entry is marked Sent. If the retries run out, the
  entry is marked failed with the error text instead of being
  reported as sent. Real API and network errors use a separate
  Api(String) variant, are still logged at error level, and behave as
  before.

Internally, post_patchwork_check now returns
Result<(), PatchworkCheckError> instead of Result<(), String>. The
error type implements Display and Error, and the worker calls
to_string() on it when recording a failure. New tests cover the error
display text. They also use a small one-shot raw-socket HTTP server to
check that a 200 response with an empty list gives NotIndexedYet and
that a 500 response gives an Api error.

findings.problem: final NotIndexedYet attempt marks row Failed, logs info
findings.explanation: Consequence: when the retry budget is exhausted on NotIndexedYet, the Patchwork check is permanently dropped and the only log line is info-level 'not ready yet', which reads as transient. Anyone alerting on error-level logs misses the lost check; the only trace is the error_log column of the Failed row. Reachability: every NotIndexedYet result passes through this arm, and the final attempt (retry_count + 1 >= max_retries) goes straight to mark_patchwork_failed. The log level is chosen from the error variant alone, before the exhaustion check, and nothing is logged on a successful mark-failed. Before the change the final failure of any error was logged at error level, and the commit's stated purpose was to stop a Patchwork check from vanishing quietly, so this reintroduces a quieter form of it. Contained: the DB row does record Failed with the message, and it is a log-level defect, not a wrong result, so Medium. The fix is to log at warn/error when the attempt is terminal.

findings.problem: NotIndexedYet retry window is only about 35s
findings.explanation: Consequence and reachability: when Patchwork's mailing-list mirror lags more than about 35 seconds behind Sashiko's review, the new NotIndexedYet path ends the outbox row as Failed. The patch then gets no check while the review email has already gone out, which is the issue 461 symptom. Every API-mode check enqueued by src/reviewer.rs (insert_patchwork_outbox) and processed by PatchworkWorker::run reaches this path. Verified in code: (1) src/main.rs:920 builds the worker with pw_max_retries = settings.review.max_retries, the same budget used by reviewer.rs and the forge worker. (2) src/settings.rs default_max_retries() is 3, and Settings.toml:217 also sets max_retries = 3, so the shipped config does not raise it. (3) In PatchworkWorker::run the error arm checks entry.retry_count + 1 >= self.max_retries. mark_patchwork_failed and set_patchwork_retry_at (src/db.rs, set_patchwork_retry_at increments retry_count) give this sequence: attempt 1 at retry_count 0 retries after backoff_seconds(0) = 5s; attempt 2 at retry_count 1 retries after 30s; attempt 3 at retry_count 2 gives 3 >= 3 and marks Failed. The total window is about 35s plus poll time, and the 180s tier in backoff_seconds is unreachable with the default cap. (4) NotIndexedYet is handled exactly like Api errors in that budget logic; only the log level differs. The commit message says Fixes #461 and calls the condition self-resolving, but nothing in the diff or in docs/ gives a measured mirror lag, and no worker-level test covers exhaustion; the new tests only cover the empty-list classification in post_patchwork_check. I could not determine the real kernel.org lag, since it depends on the external Patchwork deployment. That is why this is capped at Medium. It stays reported because the change makes a transient case retryable but does not give it a window sized to the lag. The failure is now visible in error_log instead of silent, which is an improvement, but the review-sent-without-status outcome still occurs whenever the lag exceeds the window. Confirming the actual lag, or giving NotIndexedYet its own larger retry budget, would resolve it.

findings.problem: exhausted not-indexed check is logged at info and mislabelled as lag
findings.type: Behavior Change / Permanent Not-Found Treated as Retryable
findings.explanation: Consequence and reachability: the empty-list branch cannot tell 'mirror has not caught up yet' from 'this patch will never exist on this instance'. It returns HTTP 200 with [] for both, and post_patchwork_check maps both to NotIndexedYet. In PatchworkWorker::run, every NotIndexedYet is logged at info, including the attempt that exhausts the budget (retry_count + 1 >= max_retries, default 3 from Settings.toml and settings.rs default_max_retries). That attempt calls mark_patchwork_failed and the row becomes Failed, but the only log line is 'not ready yet' at info. Only the Api variant logs at error. Reachability: api_url comes from per-subsystem or default patchwork settings in the email policy (insert_patchwork_outbox in reviewer.rs queue_notifications). Nothing in the code checked here validates that the configured instance tracks the patch's list or project. A wrong api_url, wrong project, or untracked list therefore returns 200 with []. Nothing in the code prevents it, and I could not confirm from the visible config whether any deployment is currently misconfigured. Before the commit these rows were silently marked Sent, which was a false success. Failed with an error_log is the more honest outcome, so the state change is acceptable. The problem is that the terminal failure is invisible at error level and the stored error_log says 'has not indexed this message yet', which suggests lag rather than misconfiguration. Anyone filtering logs on error will not see that a check was permanently dropped. Related effect on the same path: the backoff is 5s then 30s (backoff_seconds), so the whole retry window is about 35s. Any mirror lag longer than that also ends Failed with the same info-level log. The commit message does not mention either the permanent case or this window. The finding rests on the unverified assumption that a deployment can have an api_url that never indexes a given msgid; this is capped at Medium. Confirm by checking the deployed email_policy.toml patchwork api_url and project against the lists being reviewed. Fix: log at error (or warn) when NotIndexedYet exhausts retries, and make the stored error_log say that retries were exhausted and the patch may not be tracked by this instance.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The final, retry-exhausted attempt is logged at info while the row is permanently marked Failed, so a dropped check produces no error-level log.
Single point where 'not yet' and 'never' are conflated; a permanently untracked patch gets the same variant and message as transient lag.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: 1) The worker edit in src/worker/patchwork.rs is a log-level match on the error variant plus e.to_string() passed to mark_patchwork_failed. The retry/fail branching (retry_count + 1 >= max_retries, backoff_seconds, set_patchwork_retry_at, mark_patchwork_failed) is unchanged generic code that runs for every Err. It is not new logic, so reverting the log-level arm changes only the log level. No existing test in src/worker covers patchwork.rs (tests exist only in bug_worker, email, prefetch and prompts), so no test would fail on that revert. Under tests-that-can-fail.md this is not a finding: the behavioural change is in post_patchwork_check, and test_empty_patch_list_is_retryable_not_success fails if the empty list goes back to Ok(()), which is the actual bug. 2) The DB transitions are visible and correct for NotIndexedYet: set_patchwork_retry_at sets status Pending and retry_count = retry_count + 1 with next_retry_at; mark_patchwork_failed sets status Failed with error_log, so an entry that is never indexed ends as a recorded Failed row with 'Patchwork has not indexed this message yet', not a silent success. That outcome is bounded and visible, and the retry window is pre-existing design. 3) The 500 test asserts Err(Api(_)), which a transport error would also satisfy. This is a real weakness in the assertion, but the code under it is right: every non-2xx path returns Api, and the test's job is to show an HTTP error is not mapped to NotIndexedYet, which it does. The stub binds a real listener, so connect succeeds, and it writes a full status line with matching Content-Length. The concern points to no code defect, only a stronger assertion that could be written, which the guide says is not a finding. 4) The commit says the backoff is shared with the forge outbox worker. In fact backoff_seconds is duplicated in forge.rs and patchwork.rs with identical 5/30/180 values, and forge's is_permanent_failure is not used by the patchwork worker. The commit wording is imprecise, but the behaviour it describes (three attempts, 5s then 30s) holds and the commit makes no claim about tests, so there is no claim-versus-evidence gap that affects behaviour.
